name: IvorySQL
tagline: Apache-licensed PostgreSQL distribution with an Oracle-compatible mode, PL/iSQL and Oracle packages.
description: IvorySQL is an open-source distribution of PostgreSQL, sponsored by China's HighGo Software, that adds an Oracle compatibility layer you can switch on per instance. In Oracle mode it accepts Oracle-style syntax and data types, a PL/SQL-like procedural language (PL/iSQL), packages, built-in Oracle functions and a separate Oracle-compatible listener port, while the PostgreSQL mode stays stock. It tracks upstream closely (5.6 is based on PostgreSQL 18.6) and keeps extension compatibility, making it an open alternative to commercial Oracle-compatible Postgres builds. Compatibility coverage is still narrower than EDB's, and most of the community is in China.

scale.notes: Same scaling model as PostgreSQL: vertical plus streaming replicas.

strengths: Oracle-compatible syntax, packages and PL/iSQL under a permissive license
Switchable compatibility mode keeps a normal PostgreSQL mode available
Tracks upstream PostgreSQL minor releases quickly
Works with the standard PostgreSQL extension ecosystem
weaknesses: Oracle compatibility is less complete than commercial alternatives
Community and documentation are concentrated in China
Smaller production track record than EDB or Postgres Pro
useCases: Running Oracle-style PL/SQL code on Postgres
Teams wanting Oracle syntax without commercial licensing
notIdealFor: Apps needing near-complete Oracle behavior parity
Teams with no Oracle legacy (use stock PostgreSQL)
